title: Balanced subprotocol selection
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party protocol, let $P(\mathrm{false})$ and $P(\mathrm{true})$ be subprotocols of $p$, and let $n$ be a natural number. Suppose that three times the sum of their numbers of leaves is at least $2n$. Suppose also that for each bit $b$, whenever $3$ times the number of leaves of $P(b)$ is at least $2n$, there is a subprotocol $s$ of $P(b)$ whose number of leaves, multiplied by $3$, is at least $n$ and strictly less than $2n$. Then $p$ has a subprotocol $s$ whose number of leaves, multiplied by $3$, is at least $n$ and strictly less than $2n$.
hypotheses_covered: Each child $P(b)$ is a subprotocol of $p$
For each $b$, if $3\ell(P(b))\ge 2n$, some subprotocol $s$ of $P(b)$ satisfies $n\le 3\ell(s)<2n$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a protocol, let $P(\mathrm{false})$ and $P(\mathrm{true})$ be two protocols
that are both subprotocols of $p$, and let $n$ be a natural number with
$3\,(\ell(P(\mathrm{false})) + \ell(P(\mathrm{true}))) \ge 2n$, where $\ell(\cdot)$ denotes
the number of leaves. Suppose further that for each bit $b$ with $3\,\ell(P(b)) \ge 2n$
there is a subprotocol $s$ of $P(b)$ with $n \le 3\,\ell(s) < 2n$. Then there is a
subprotocol $s$ of $p$ with $n \le 3\,\ell(s) < 2n$.
